transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve just felt really down. It’s like this heavy, sad feeling sitting on me most of the day. Even at work, I can smile and talk to patients, but inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together.
How many weeks exactly have you been feeling this heavy, sad feeling?
About three weeks now. It started not long after I found out I was pregnant.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

Yeah. I used to paint after work, or go to yoga or salsa classes to kind of unwind. Lately I just go home after my shift and sit on the couch. I don’t even answer texts sometimes. It all just feels like too much effort, or like there’s no point.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you do, even if you don't feel like doing them?

Not really. Even if I try to start painting or think about going to yoga or salsa, it just doesn’t feel good the way it used to. After work I mostly just go home, sit on the couch, and I’ll ignore texts because none of it feels worth the effort.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to be alive or of harming yourself?

Yes… I’ve had thoughts like I wish I just wouldn’t wake up. That’s actually what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but the thoughts are there.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure about the exact number, but my appetite has definitely changed. I know I should be eating regularly, especially being pregnant, but most days food just doesn’t sound good. I’ll get halfway through a clinic shift and realize I’ve only had coffee or some crackers all day.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done physically since you started feeling down?

Yes. Everything feels slower than it should, like I’m moving through syrup. Even simple stuff at the clinic, like getting wound supplies together or finishing my charting, takes me way longer than it normally would.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, since you started feeling down?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there. It’s more just… feeling really low, not like I’m losing touch with reality.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still since you started feeling down?
Not really restless, no. It’s more the opposite — I feel slowed down. Like even basic things at work, getting supplies together or finishing my charting, take me a lot longer than they should.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular since you've been feeling down?
I don’t think there’s anything specific. I mean, I feel bad about not keeping up with things the way I usually do, but it’s not like one particular thing I’m guilty about.
Have you been experiencing any difficulty concentrating or making decisions since you started feeling down?

Yes. I’ve been having a hard time focusing. At work I keep rereading medication orders and wound-care notes because my brain feels foggy, like it doesn’t sink in the first time. And decisions I’d normally make without thinking… now I freeze up and second-guess myself.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and lack of interest in activities are present most of the day, or are there times when you feel somewhat better?

It’s there most of the day. I might get through a conversation or smile at a patient at work, but inside it still feels like this heavy sadness is just sitting on me. I don’t really feel like myself, and it feels like I’m barely holding it together.
Would you say your low mood and other symptoms are interfering with your ability to work or take care of yourself at home?

Yes. I’m still getting myself to work, but it’s definitely affecting me. My supervisor has already noticed some incomplete charting, which is embarrassing. And at home… I’m not really keeping up the way I normally would. I’ve also been pulling away from friends and the things that usually help keep me steady.
Have you had any days in the past week where you felt somewhat better, or has the sadness been constant?

It’s been pretty constant. There might be little moments where I’m distracted, like if I’m talking to someone at work, but the sadness doesn’t really lift. It feels like this heavy pressure is there almost all day, and I’m just trying to keep myself together.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness are severe enough to interfere with your relationships with others?

Yes, I think so. I’ve been pulling away from friends, even the people I usually lean on. I’m still getting to work, but my supervisor has noticed I’m behind on charting, so it’s spilling over there too. I’m just not keeping up with people or things the way I normally would.
Would you describe your current feelings of sadness as being moderately severe or very severe?
I’d say moderately severe. It’s been this heavy sadness most of the day for the past few weeks, and even when I’m smiling at patients at work, inside I feel like I’m barely holding it together.
Have there been any days in the past two weeks where you felt almost back to your normal self?

No, not really. Maybe I can seem okay for a little while at work, like when I’m smiling with patients, but inside that heavy sadness is still there. I haven’t felt like my normal self these past couple weeks.
Would you say your sadness is worse in the morning or does it stay about the same throughout the day?

It’s more like it stays with me most of the day. I don’t really notice it being especially worse in the morning—just this heavy sadness that’s kind of sitting on me almost all day, even when I’m at work trying to smile and act normal.
Would you say that your current feelings of sadness are getting worse over time?

It’s hard to say if it’s getting worse day by day, but it has been hanging on for the past few weeks. It feels like this heavy sad pressure most of the day, and even when I’m at work smiling at patients, inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.
Would you say your sadness is affecting your daily life in a mild way or a more significant way?

It’s more significant than mild. I’m still getting myself to work, but I’m not keeping up the way I usually do—my supervisor has noticed some of my charting isn’t getting finished. And outside of work I’ve been pulling away from friends and the things that normally help keep me steady.
